From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Audit logs / data access - follow up and export samples

Hi Emily / Finco team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion and appreciate the clarity on your compliance bar. Per our call, quick recap of the items you asked us to provide so your security and compliance teams can validate Redwood for the pilot: 

- Audit log scope: who accessed what/when (user/actor id, role, operation, resource path, timestamp)
- Export formats: CSV and JSON samples showing typical schema
- PII handling: whether identifiers are raw/de-identified/hashed; options for redaction or tokenization
- Retention: default retention and configurable retention windows (12/24/36 months) and legal hold options
- Data residency: confirmation of EU/US region controls for logs and exports
- Evidence: short extract (redacted) covering last 12 months for review by auditors

I'm attaching our SOC2 controls matrix as context. Sean and Laura from our team are copied — Sean will prepare export samples and the retention policy, Laura will confirm the PII/redaction behavior. Can you confirm the preferred export delivery method (SFTP, secure Drive link, or encrypted email) and whether you need a signed attestation?

Next step: we'll send the export sample + retention doc by end of day tomorrow and a proposed timeline for a secured extract.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachment: soc2-controls-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks Marissa — that matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from the security team before you send samples: 

1) Are user identifiers in the logs stored as raw customer IDs, or are they hashed/pseudonymized by default? We need to know whether exported logs will include PII that requires extra handling.
2) For exports, do you include payloads or only metadata (i.e., are request/response contents ever present in the audit exports)?
3) Preferred delivery: SFTP is preferred for initial samples; we can provide an account/credentials if needed.

If you can include those details with the sample that would be ideal. We may need a quick one-pager on retention settings for our auditors.

—Emily Soto
Director, InfoSec | FincoBank
emily.soto@fincobank.com

Marissa / team — attaching the sample exports and a short retention summary. Summary highlights: 

- Sample exports attached: audit_export_sample.csv, audit_export_sample.json (both redacted)
- actor_id is hashed by default for hosted tenants; we can provide hashed IDs (SHA256) or customer-provided tokenization on Dedicated/Private deployments
- request/response payloads are NOT included in standard audit export; only metadata. We can include payloads under special request with additional controls and approvals.
- Default retention: 12 months; configurable to 24 / 36 months via admin console. Legal-hold snapshots supported for enterprise forensics.
- Exports are available via SFTP, signed-expiring Drive link, or secure API endpoint.

I'll attach the files to the thread for sharing with Finco after Laura signs off on the hashing description.

Attachments: audit_export_sample.csv (CSV stub), audit_export_sample.json (JSON stub), retention_policy.pdf (policy summary)

Hi Emily — thanks for the questions. Per internal thread below, summary and next steps: 

- PII / identifiers: actor_id is hashed by default for hosted customers (SHA256). We can also support customer-provided tokens for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Payloads: standard audit exports include metadata only (no request/response payloads). Payload inclusion is available on a case-by-case basis with controls.
- Export formats: attached are redacted samples in CSV and JSON (audit_export_sample.csv, audit_export_sample.json).
- Retention: default 12 months; configurable to 24/36 months. Legal-hold snapshots available for enterprise investigations. See attached retention_policy.pdf for details.
- Delivery: we can place samples on SFTP (send credentials) or provide an expiring signed Drive link. Let us know which you prefer.

Next steps: if SFTP is preferred, please send instructions/target and we will upload the samples and a short README. If you need a formal signed attestation, let me know and I will route to our legal team.
